explanation:
The main function is the entry point of any C program, where execution begins. It is essential because it serves as the starting point for the program to run, allowing the operating system to call it when the program is executed. In UNIX-standardized C environments, adhering to the standard signature ensures portability and compatibility across systems.

The main function in C is the entry point of a program, where execution begins when the program is run by the operating system. It is essential because it allows the program to start executing code, process inputs, perform tasks, and return an exit status, making it a fundamental structure for all C programs.
example_explanation: This example defines the main function as the program's starting point. When executed, it prints 'Hello, world!' to the console using printf, demonstrating how the main function runs the code inside its block and returns 0 to indicate successful completion.
